知情人士透露，英伟达CEO黄仁勋(Jensen Huang)周一走进了公司位于加州圣克拉拉的总部，照常主持了与高层管理人员的晨会。

知情人士称，黄仁勋在这场闭门会议开始时首先就最近的风波向员工表达了歉意。他没有接受任何提问，而是很快将话题转向业务和当天的主要议程。

周二，黄仁勋也来到办公室开会。还有一周时间，英伟达就将发布新一季财报。

items.body:
Claude封号新规11月12日生效：美国人来华也受限，中国企业在海外也受限

Anthropic 新版《支持地区政策》将于 11 月 12 日生效。新文件明确了三类禁止使用 Claude 的情况，覆盖个人、企业，以及通过海外公司和第三方云平台使用模型的用户。

第一，只要人处于不支持地区，就不能使用 Claude。即使是美国人，到中国大陆出差期间使用 Claude，同样违反规定。

第二，只要公司注册地或总部位于中国大陆等不支持地区，哪怕员工人在美国，也不能使用 Claude 为这家公司工作。

第三，即使公司注册在美国，只要被不支持地区的个人或企业直接、间接控股或控制，员工同样受到限制，并非只有持股超过 50% 才会触发。

政策覆盖 Claude.ai、Claude Code、Cowork、官方 API，以及云平台和授权经销商提供的 Claude 模型。通过 AWS Bedrock 等正规云平台调用模型，也不意味着可以绕过地区使用限制。

但这并非 11 月 12 日才突然推出的全面封禁。Anthropic 早在 2025 年 9 月就已禁止受中国等不支持地区企业控股的海外公司使用 Claude。这次主要把个人所在地、企业注册地和控制关系写得更加明确。

Anthropic 的封号行动早已开始。官方披露，2026 年上半年共封禁 1140 万个账号，收到 39.8 万次申诉，其中 4.2 万次成功推翻原决定。这些数据涵盖各类违规行为，并非全部涉及地区限制。

Anthropic 之前还披露，系统会识别来自不支持地区、未经授权转售 Claude 等风险信号，并要求相关用户验证身份，验证失败就会封号。11 月 12 日之后，地区和企业归属规则将有更明确的正式文本可供执行。

items.title: 华为新型存储系统11月12日启动试用，瞄准AI温冷数据
items.summary: 华为将于周四在贵州贵安云上屯启动新型存储系统试用，推动相关技术由实验室验证进入客户真实场景的联合验证阶段。该系统主要面向大模型数据集、媒体资料归档、备份容灾和科研数据等大规模温冷数据场景。 所谓温冷数据，是指访问频率相对较低、但需要长期保存并可能被重新调用的数据。华为此次试用的新型存储系统搭载自研磁电盘MED，通过“电场控磁”技术替代传统硬盘的“电流生磁”方式。其目标是在存储成本接近磁带的同时，提供接近机械硬盘的数据取回能力，在成本、能耗和访问效率之间寻找新的平衡。 —— 凤凰网科技
items.body:
华为新型存储系统11月12日启动试用，瞄准AI温冷数据

华为将于周四在贵州贵安云上屯启动新型存储系统试用，推动相关技术由实验室验证进入客户真实场景的联合验证阶段。该系统主要面向大模型数据集、媒体资料归档、备份容灾和科研数据等大规模温冷数据场景。

所谓温冷数据，是指访问频率相对较低、但需要长期保存并可能被重新调用的数据。华为此次试用的新型存储系统搭载自研磁电盘MED，通过“电场控磁”技术替代传统硬盘的“电流生磁”方式。其目标是在存储成本接近磁带的同时，提供接近机械硬盘的数据取回能力，在成本、能耗和访问效率之间寻找新的平衡。

—— 凤凰网科技

美国联邦通信委员会正在研究相关限制，但尚未公布最终规则。美国政府提出限制的理由是，中国制造的新型号光模块可能被用于窃取数据、植入恶意软件或干扰数据中心服务。消息人士称，FCC正在考虑将传输速率达到3.2Tbps的中国光模块纳入限制范围。

items.body:
MiniMax H3生图模型正式开源：6步直出1680万像素，社区已抢跑一周

MiniMax 正式发布 H3-Image 并开源模型权重。它可以直接生成 4096×4096、约 1680 万像素的图片，无需额外放大。按照官方数据，生成时间不到 10 秒，速度最高达到主流产品的 5 倍。它还把文生图、图片编辑整合进同一个模型，最多支持 16 张参考图。

H3-Image 沿用了 H3 视频模型的架构，去掉音频部分，保留原有的文本编码器，并为图片重新设计了解码器。核心图像生成网络有 331 亿参数。经过蒸馏，生成一张图片只需 6 次采样，大幅减少了计算步骤。

这款模型其实早在 8 月就已经预告过。8 月 7 日，MiniMax 研究员 Kiro 在 Reddit AMA 中透露，团队正在从 H3 的同源架构开发专用图像模型，并计划开源权重。当时还提出了一套工作流程：先用图像模型生成首帧，再交给 H3 继续生成视频。

社区甚至抢在 MiniMax 前面做了出来。11 月 3 日，Pruna AI 就基于开源的 H3 视频模型推出 P-H3-Image，同样支持生图和修图。Pruna 将生成网络从 331 亿压缩至约 200 亿参数，只需 8 步采样。最小量化版本约 20GB，生成 800 万像素图片时，峰值显存仅约 21GB。

MiniMax 官方版则保留了 331 亿参数的生成网络，将采样进一步压缩到 6 步，并支持更高分辨率和更多参考图。不过，原始权重加上复用的文本编码器一共约 135GB 明显更重。

H3-Image 的开源权重许可存在限制。美国、英国、欧盟和韩国不在社区许可证的授权地区内。企业年化营收超过 100 万美元，或者向第三方提供模型托管服务，都需要事先获得单独授权。

items.body:
Anthropic路演披露长期经营利润率目标为35%或以上，算力支出占比目标降至45%至50%

Anthropic 在 11 月 10 日公布的 IPO 路演视频中披露，公司相信长期能够实现 35% 或以上的调整后经营利润率，高于 2026 年第三季度的 15%，但未给出明确实现时间表。

Anthropic 首席财务官 Krishna Rao 表示，公司计划通过提升算力效率、增加直接租赁芯片和数据中心的比例，以及扩大推理业务占比，改善长期成本结构。计算与基础设施支出占营收的比例，目标从第三季度的 58% 降至 45% 至 50%；销售、营销及合作伙伴费用占比拟由 14% 降至 7% 至 10%，经调整的人员及其他运营费用占比拟由 13% 降至 7% 至 10%。

客户方面，截至 9 月底，过去 12 个月为 Anthropic 贡献超过 10 万美元营收的企业客户逾 11,900 家，其中贡献超过 100 万美元的客户逾 1900 家、超过 1000 万美元的客户约 250 家。企业客户净收入留存率约 900%，超过一半的企业客户同时使用 Claude Platform 及至少一款 Anthropic 自有应用。路演还展示了礼来、乐天、Salesforce 和沃尔玛等客户的应用案例。

算力效率方面，Anthropic 使用营收与计算及基础设施支出的比值衡量，该指标从 2025 年第一季度的 0.40 倍升至 2026 年第三季度的 1.72 倍，约为此前的 4.3 倍，但低于第二季度的 2.08 倍。公司称，第三季度使用了约 50 亿美元的短期算力，其成本明显高于多年期协议采购的算力。

实际业绩方面，Anthropic 第三季度营收 169.56 亿美元，调整后经营利润 24.63 亿美元，调整后经营利润率 15%，低于第二季度的 19%。按 GAAP 口径，公司第三季度仍录得 5.67 亿美元经营亏损。调整后指标剔除了股权激励、非现金慈善捐赠等费用，不能等同于 GAAP 盈利。截至 10 月底，公司年化营收运行率约 810 亿美元，并非已实现的全年营收。

此外，Anthropic 披露长期算力及基础设施承诺约 9000 亿美元，其中约 4516 亿美元预计在 2030 年底前发生，未来 12 个月到期的相关承诺约 707 亿美元。截至第三季度末，公司持有约 960 亿美元现金及现金等价物、约 360 亿美元短期投资。

items.body:
谷歌最强模型Gemini 4 Carbon正式开放，安全团队2小时挖出全新零日漏洞

谷歌正式面向普通用户开放 Gemini 4 Carbon。之前两周只有少数网络安全团队能够试用，现在所有付费开发者都可以通过 API 调用。Google AI Ultra 用户也能在 Gemini、搜索 AI 模式和 Antigravity 中使用，Pro 和免费用户暂时不支持。

谷歌还披露了一项实际应用案例。旗下网络安全公司 Wiz 使用 Carbon 检查两家大型软件服务商，在不到两小时内发现了全新的零日漏洞，并协助企业修复。谷歌称，这类漏洞研究过去通常需要数周。

不过，Wiz 使用的是专门的网络安全版本 Carbon for cyber，目前仍需申请 Fairwind 计划才能访问。这次向普通用户开放的是通用版。

API 首发价为每百万 Token 输入 2 美元、输出 10 美元，与 Argon 相同。优惠只持续到 11 月 30 日，之后价格翻倍。

谷歌表示，Carbon 适合复杂编程、深度调试和科研任务，会花费更多 Token 反复推理和验证。多数日常工作仍推荐使用 Argon。

Anthropic承销商考虑上调IPO发行价，目标估值或升至1.5万亿美元以上

据英国《金融时报》援引知情人士报道，Anthropic 的 IPO 路演获得强劲认购意向，高盛和摩根士丹利牵头的承销团队正考虑将发行价上调至每股 78 美元以上，目标估值可能在未来几天升至 1.5 万亿美元或更高。Anthropic 预计下周上市，最终发行价尚未确定。

Anthropic 周二提交的文件显示，初步发行价区间为每股 70 至 78 美元，按完全摊薄口径计算，对应估值为 1.26 万亿至 1.41 万亿美元。按原方案，IPO 基础募资规模最高约 640 亿美元，若行使超额配售权，可再募资近 100 亿美元。谷歌、英伟达和微软等战略伙伴还将按 IPO 发行价参与私募配售，合计投资 260 亿美元。报道称，若发行价上调，计入配套融资后的总募资额可能超过 1000 亿美元。

三名 Anthropic 投资者表示，公司目前更关注通过上市筹集尽可能多的资金，以支持算力支出，而非追求最高估值。Anthropic 计划未来数年在算力和基础设施上投入约 9000 亿美元，并向投资者披露，10 月年化营收达到 810 亿美元，第三季度营收为 170 亿美元。晨星分析师认为，其公允股权价值约为 1.7 万亿美元，但视 AI 工具的普及速度而定，估值可能介于 5000 亿至 3 万亿美元之间。

部分投资者也开始向其他买家推介部分 IPO 配售股份。《金融时报》看到的消息显示，一家纽约经纪商正代表一家风投机构推介至多 5 亿美元的股份，报价较最终 IPO 发行价高 4%。另有一家风投机构通过特殊目的载体（SPV）推介价值 12.5 亿美元的股份，对应公司估值 1.5 万亿美元。Anthropic 此前警告，不会认可部分上市前二级市场经纪商提出的转售要约。

items.title: JioStar’s chief architect on AI discovery at 500M-user scale
items.summary: JioStar’s Vijay Seshadri explains AI discovery at 500M-user scale. Read his lessons on evals, guardrails, and taking AI into production.
items.body:
November 11, 2026

A conversation with Vijay Seshadri, Chief Architect at JioStar.

Contact sales

Company size: Enterprise

Region: Asia-Pacific & Oceania

Industry: Media, Entertainment & Sport

Products: API, Codex

Our Executive Function series features perspectives from leaders driving transformation through AI.

JioStar operates entertainment and live-sports platforms used by more than 500 million consumers and has supported as many as 72.5 million concurrent live-sports viewers. At that scale, AI has to be fast, reliable, and ready for production.

Using the OpenAI API, JioStar built a conversational video and cricket-stat discovery assistant into JioHotstar. Viewers can speak naturally to find movies and shows, historical highlights, live-match moments, or cricket statistics, with results returned through a visual, conversational experience.

At OpenAI’s Executive Summit in Singapore, Sidharth Sharma, OpenAI’s Head of Go-to-Market for ASEAN, spoke with Vijay Seshadri—Chief Architect, JioStar, about building the experience for more than 15 languages in about eight weeks, and the lessons for leaders taking AI from demo to production.

Content discovery has evolved very little in the past 25 years. Recommendations were the last major shift. Much of what followed has been an iteration of the same idea.

But choosing what to watch is deeply personal. A person might say, “I’m feeling sad. Show me something that will cheer me up.” Even that simple request contains a lot of nuance. What kind of sad? What usually cheers that person up? Do they want comedy, comfort viewing or something completely distracting?

A traditional recommendation system may struggle to understand that moment. Conversation gives the viewer a way to explain it. We call this a voice-visual interface.

“Content discovery is inherently visual, but combining those visual options with spoken preferences and conversation creates a powerful new paradigm.”

—Vijay Seshadri, Chief Architect, JioStar

Listen

We began working through the concept in October and November, with a major cricket tournament coming in February. We had roughly two months and two very different audiences: entertainment viewers and cricket fans.

An entertainment viewer might say, “It’s Friday evening—surprise me,” or describe a movie without knowing its title. Sports viewers may want a more specific update, like fall of wickets, a series of sixes, or the match in which a player scored a certain number of runs. Cricket experts may want statistics about every ball.

These are very different discovery problems. We worked on bringing entertainment, sports moments and detailed cricket statistics into one experience, across multiple languages, in a very short period.

Very early, we framed the problem as a three-way tradeoff among accuracy, latency, and cost. Every engineering decision had to balance all three at once.

Voice made that especially important. More than 60% of our users use voice rather than text: people prefer to say what they want to watch. The response still has to be relevant, fast, and economically viable at scale.

“As much of a cliché as it may sound, the answer is evals, evals, and evals. If you are building an application like this for the first time, you will probably underestimate the importance of evals even if you think you are prepared.”

—Vijay Seshadri, Chief Architect, JioStar

Listen

I think about it in two parts: an evaluation framework and a validation layer. Before production, the evaluation framework should prompt changes. In production, a feedback loop should turn customer behavior and failures into new eval cases.

That flywheel can become self-amplified, but it is extremely difficult to get right.

Domain experts are essential. For sports-statistics evals, we worked with people such as sports-magazine editors who understood what serious fans might ask. You cannot begin with a prompt alone; you need to seed the system with deep human expertise.

One thing we got right was the team. We started with a small team of data scientists and engineers around a clear problem statement. OpenAI’s forward-deployed engineers worked alongside us to further identify the few things we absolutely had to get right.

The first was scope. A voice or text interface lets users ask almost anything, so we began by deciding what the system should not answer. Guardrails came first.

For evals, we began with a seed dataset and used models to expand it with more variation. We created what you might now call a maker-checker pattern: one model helped determine how to answer a question, while another acted as a validator—an LLM as judge—with a competing objective.

That raised another question: who tests the judge? Designing the validator was itself an evaluation problem. Codex helped the team accelerate work such as generating eval cases and updating the system, but faster building did not remove the need for judgment and validation.

I would invest earlier in production monitoring for model efficacy.

Traditional infrastructure measures such as P99 latency remain important, but they are not enough. You also need to monitor model efficacy in production.

First, there is a large gap between what technology can do and the reality inside an enterprise. If your company has not matched every frontier-model announcement, you are not alone.

Second, keep focusing on outcomes rather than activity. It is easy to mistake visible motion for meaningful progress, particularly when companies emphasize input metrics. Lines of code generated, for example, do not tell you whether you created meaningful value.

“I see AI as a massive simplification hammer for the enterprise. If we do not use it to simplify business processes, workflows, and software-engineering systems, it will be a huge wasted opportunity.”

—Vijay Seshadri, Chief Architect, JioStar

Listen

Finally, most enterprises underestimate the human skill and agency required. This cannot be only a generic skilling program. Leaders need people who can apply these tools with judgment. Give a strong engineer a tool like Codex and the impact can multiply; without the judgment to validate production systems, the risk multiplies too.

You have a rocket in your hands. Especially in production systems, you need validation and guardrails, and you need to give the keys to the right people.

A traditional recommendation system may struggle to understand that moment. Conversation gives the viewer a way to explain it. We call this a voice-visual interface.
“Content discovery is inherently visual, but combining those visual options with spoken preferences and conversation creates a powerful new paradigm.”
—Vijay Seshadri, Chief Architect, JioStar
Listen

We began working through the concept in October and November, with a major cricket tournament coming in February. We had roughly two months and two very different audiences: entertainment viewers and cricket fans.

An entertainment viewer might say, “It’s Friday evening—surprise me,” or describe a movie without knowing its title. Sports viewers may want a more specific update, like fall of wickets, a series of sixes, or the match in which a player scored a certain number of runs. Cricket experts may want statistics about every ball.

These are very different discovery problems. We worked on bringing entertainment, sports moments and detailed cricket statistics into one experience, across multiple languages, in a very short period.
Very early, we framed the problem as a three-way tradeoff among accuracy, latency, and cost. Every engineering decision had to balance all three at once.

Voice made that especially important. More than 60% of our users use voice rather than text: people prefer to say what they want to watch. The response still has to be relevant, fast, and economically viable at scale.

“As much of a cliché as it may sound, the answer is evals, evals, and evals. If you are building an application like this for the first time, you will probably underestimate the importance of evals even if you think you are prepared.”
—Vijay Seshadri, Chief Architect, JioStar
Listen

I think about it in two parts: an evaluation framework and a validation layer. Before production, the evaluation framework should prompt changes. In production, a feedback loop should turn customer behavior and failures into new eval cases.
That flywheel can become self-amplified, but it is extremely difficult to get right.

Domain experts are essential. For sports-statistics evals, we worked with people such as sports-magazine editors who understood what serious fans might ask. You cannot begin with a prompt alone; you need to seed the system with deep human expertise.

One thing we got right was the team. We started with a small team of data scientists and engineers around a clear problem statement. OpenAI’s forward-deployed engineers worked alongside us to further identify the few things we absolutely had to get right.
The first was scope. A voice or text interface lets users ask almost anything, so we began by deciding what the system should not answer. Guardrails came first.

For evals, we began with a seed dataset and used models to expand it with more variation. We created what you might now call a maker-checker pattern: one model helped determine how to answer a question, while another acted as a validator—an LLM as judge—with a competing objective.

That raised another question: who tests the judge? Designing the validator was itself an evaluation problem. Codex helped the team accelerate work such as generating eval cases and updating the system, but faster building did not remove the need for judgment and validation.
I would invest earlier in production monitoring for model efficacy.
Traditional infrastructure measures such as P99 latency remain important, but they are not enough. You also need to monitor model efficacy in production.
First, there is a large gap between what technology can do and the reality inside an enterprise. If your company has not matched every frontier-model announcement, you are not alone.

Second, keep focusing on outcomes rather than activity. It is easy to mistake visible motion for meaningful progress, particularly when companies emphasize input metrics. Lines of code generated, for example, do not tell you whether you created meaningful value.

“I see AI as a massive simplification hammer for the enterprise. If we do not use it to simplify business processes, workflows, and software-engineering systems, it will be a huge wasted opportunity.”
—Vijay Seshadri, Chief Architect, JioStar
Listen

Finally, most enterprises underestimate the human skill and agency required. This cannot be only a generic skilling program. Leaders need people who can apply these tools with judgment. Give a strong engineer a tool like Codex and the impact can multiply; without the judgment to validate production systems, the risk multiplies too.
You have a rocket in your hands. Especially in production systems, you need validation and guardrails, and you need to give the keys to the right people.

🤖 Claude 为付费用户提供一次免费额度重置

Claude 为 Pro、Max、Ultra 和 Team 用户各提供一次免费全量重置，涵盖所有模型和使用限额，可在太平洋时间 12 月 10 日下午 2 点前使用。用户可在“设置 > 用量”中找到该选项，也可访问 clau.de/reset。

Claude 表示，此举是为补偿近期少数问题造成的影响：部分问题曾导致限额消耗超出预期，Fable 重置也未能帮助已用完所有模型每周限额的用户。
